scope.limits: Named mathematical statements in the active maintained source closure, plus separately listed load-bearing supporting claims. This is not a claim to mechanically prove every prose sentence, empirical assumption, archived draft, or numerical implementation.

review_method.manual: Read all 13 active statements and their complete printed proofs; checked boundary/degenerate cases and inspected referenced Lean declaration types and proofs. No fresh Lean kernel run was performed by this inventory reviewer. Root integration must bind any later run separately.

formal_status_meanings.scoped_mechanization: Relevant mathematical core is mechanized under explicitly identified representation/support premises; exact printed-to-Lean instantiation steps remain described.
formal_status_meanings.partial_mechanization: Only components or a narrower special case are mechanized; the complete printed statement has a manually reviewed proof.
formal_status_meanings.latex_only: The printed proof was reviewed manually; no exact registered counterpart is claimed.

statements.title: Label-kernel freedom on disagreement
assumptions: Binary labels and zero-one loss
Fixed measurable model pair and score s in [0,1]
Positive target disagreement mass d
Measurable target correctness kernel
Fixed input law, source information, and off-disagreement label kernel
Every measurable correctness kernel on disagreement is admitted
statements.conclusion: Every measurable correctness field on disagreement induces a target law with unchanged label-free input/model-output law and gamma=E[eta|D]-1/2-M.

proof_authority.summary: Patch the two predicted-label point masses on D with the fixed Markov kernel outside D. Integrate against the unchanged input law. Measurable pushforwards of input evidence are unchanged.

formal_correspondence.boundary: The Lean declarations construct actual measurable joint laws and single-input measurable evidence pushforwards. Product-sample and independent-source-evidence lifting in the printed batch wording is a manual correspondence step; no arbitrary restricted deployment class is asserted rich.

edge_cases: On agreement the off-D law is unchanged.
At eta=0 or eta=1 the conditional distribution remains valid.
Binary prediction disagreement ensures the two support atoms differ.

statements.title: Disagreement-region reduction
assumptions: Binary labels and zero-one loss
Fixed measurable model pair and score s in [0,1]
Positive target disagreement mass d
Measurable target correctness kernel
statements.conclusion: Delta=2d(E[eta|D]-1/2)=2d(M+gamma), and the signs agree; no beta bound is needed for the identity.

proof_authority.summary: The paired zero-one accuracy contrast is zero off D and 2 eta-1 on D. Integrating and using d>0 yields the equality and sign result.

formal_correspondence.boundary: Lean covers laws constructed from the measurable two-prediction kernel. Representing an arbitrary binary target law with its assumed conditional kernel is a manual correspondence step. Neither the printed nor formal reduction extends to arbitrary multiclass labels on disagreement.

edge_cases: d=0 is outside the conditional definition; its unconditional benefit is zero.
M+gamma=0 gives Delta=0.
No source calibration property is required.

statements.title: Interior matched-evidence impossibility
assumptions: Binary labels and zero-one loss
Fixed measurable model pair and score s in [0,1]
Positive target disagreement mass d
Measurable target correctness kernel
Full measurable correctness-kernel class with fixed observables
beta>0 and feasible |M|<beta
Evidence contains no target-label information
statements.conclusion: Two laws in C_beta have identical augmented evidence and opposite nonzero population benefit.

proof_authority.summary: Choose 0<delta<min(beta-|M|,1/2), set eta=1/2 +/- delta, and keep the rest of the kernel fixed. Residual magnitudes are strictly below beta, and benefits are +/- 2d delta.

formal_correspondence.boundary: The full constructed measurable kernel class is covered. Batch/source-evidence lifting and matching the score-defined M to the Lean real parameter are manual instantiation steps. The result does not assert richness of a restricted real deployment class.

edge_cases: beta=0 admits no such interior pair.
|M|=beta is not an opposite-nonzero-sign case.
Large beta is allowed; correctness is kept in [0,1].

statements.title: Matched-evidence abstention lower bound
assumptions: The opposite-benefit matched-evidence worlds of lem:nonid
A fixed measurable three-action rule, with independent identically distributed rule randomization across worlds
Both marginal directional errors are at most alpha in every admissible world
0<alpha<1/2
statements.conclusion: On the shared evidence law, abstention probability is at least 1-2 alpha.

proof_authority.summary: Equal evidence and randomization laws imply the same action probabilities. The negative world bounds adapt mass, the positive world bounds freeze mass, and the remainder is abstention.

formal_correspondence.boundary: The registered counterparts prove deterministic forced abstention and real-number probability arithmetic. They do not by themselves encode the full randomized rule, common probability-law pushforward, and both marginal error premises in one measure-level capstone.

edge_cases: The bound may reach zero as alpha approaches 1/2.
It is a marginal abstention lower bound, not a regret bound or acceptance-conditional error statement.

statements.title: Boundary case and closed-band abstention
assumptions: Binary labels and zero-one loss
Fixed measurable model pair and score s in [0,1]
Positive target disagreement mass d
Measurable target correctness kernel
Full rich class C_beta; beta>=0
Strict directional soundness counts zero benefit as insufficient for commitment
Both marginal directional errors controlled at 0<alpha<1/2 for the probability clause
statements.conclusion: No uniformly sound strict action exists when |M|<=beta; dual marginal error control forces abstention probability at least 1-2 alpha.

proof_authority.summary: The interior has opposite-sign worlds. On |M|=beta>0 choose eta=1/2 for the zero world and eta=M+1/2 for the sign-M world. The zero world counts either commitment as directional error. For beta=M=0 every benefit is zero.

formal_correspondence.boundary: The zero-target witness and strict-frontier statements are mechanized. The randomized probability clause has the same measure-level assembly gap as cor:matched-abstain.

edge_cases: Zero-versus-strict witnesses at the boundary replace opposite-nonzero witnesses.
M=beta=0 remains abstention under strict-sign semantics although task risks tie.
Large beta still admits eta=1/2 as a zero witness.

statements.title: Exact strict-commitment frontier
assumptions: Binary labels and zero-one loss
Fixed measurable model pair and score s in [0,1]
Positive target disagreement mass d
Measurable target correctness kernel
Feasible M in [-1/2,1/2] and beta>=0
Fixed observables and the full correctness-kernel class for necessity/maximality
Strict directional semantics
statements.conclusion: A strict population action is uniformly sound exactly when |M|>beta; the sign is sign(M). The identified benefit set is the clipped interval stated immediately after the proof.

proof_authority.summary: Sufficiency is M+gamma retaining sign when |gamma|<=beta<|M|. Necessity follows from the interior opposite worlds and boundary zero world. Constant correctness kernels attain each point of the clipped interval.

formal_correspondence.boundary: Lean proves exact strict frontiers for the full constructed measurable correctness-field class, with M as a feasible real parameter. Mapping the printed score-defined M and arbitrary binary-kernel representation is manual. Only sufficiency transfers automatically to a narrower class.

edge_cases: Clipping is needed for |M| near 1/2 or large beta.
beta=0 with M!=0 identifies a strict direction.
|M|=beta always allows zero benefit.
For beta>1/2, feasible M cannot lie outside the band.

statements.title: Exact label-free audit floor
assumptions: Nonempty fibre of target laws sharing the entire observable W law
A single measurable nonnegative audit beta_hat=g(W,U), with fixed independent randomization law
0<=delta<1 and valid residual upper coverage for every law in the fibre
Residual gamma is bounded (here |gamma|<=1)
statements.conclusion: Pr(beta_hat>=sup_fibre |gamma|)>=1-delta; the constant supremum is a valid oracle bound.

proof_authority.summary: Take attainable absolute residuals increasing to Gamma. All worlds give the same audit distribution, so every threshold event has probability at least 1-delta. These events decrease to {beta_hat>=Gamma}; continuity from above yields the bound. Gamma=0 follows from nonnegativity.

formal_correspondence.boundary: No exact fibre-supremum/continuity-of-measure statement is registered in Lean. This is a manually reviewed mathematical proof, not a finite-data procedure for learning the observable law or Gamma.

edge_cases: Supremum need not be attained; the sequence argument covers it.
Nonempty fibre prevents undefined empty-class interpretation.
For Gamma=0 nonnegativity gives the result directly.
delta=0 is allowed.

statements.title: Coverage-to-action implication
assumptions: Finite real measurable B and Bhat on a common probability space
Measurable nonnegative possibly infinite radius
Marginal coverage at least 1-alpha with 0<alpha<1
Strict thresholding and no use of the new evaluation labels to select prediction/radius
statements.conclusion: Both marginal wrong-direction probabilities are at most alpha; their union is also contained in the same coverage failure event.

proof_authority.summary: On coverage, an interval strictly above zero cannot contain B<=0, and an interval strictly below zero cannot contain B>=0. At infinite radius no strict action is possible.

formal_correspondence.boundary: The new module directly encodes arbitrary measurable random extended-nonnegative radii and finite real prediction/benefit maps. Infinity explicitly abstains before toReal conversion; both errors share one coverage-failure event. Marginal coverage is still a premise; label-blind construction, real-data coverage validity, conditional-on-selection error and repeated-use validity are not proved. The primary bounds permit outer measures; under the printed measurable maps, the interval-defined error events are measurable.

edge_cases: Zero endpoint leads to abstention.
Infinite radius gives universal containment for finite B/Bhat and abstention.
B=0 makes any commitment a strict-direction error.
Marginal control gives neither error conditional on ADAPT nor automatic repeated-use/candidate-selection protection.
manual_review.new_formal_module_review: Independently read the complete new module, checking infinity conversion, strict zero boundaries, event containment, joint error budget, measurability helper and no hidden independence requirement. No defect found. Fresh kernel verification is separately receipt-bound.

statements.title: Cell-to-population transfer via compound bound
assumptions: Positive integer m; frozen pair before m fresh conditionally iid evaluation observations
Paired zero-one accuracy variables W in [-1,1] with conditional mean Delta
Valid marginal coverage of cell benefit by predictor/radius
Sampling budget delta in (0,1); declared cell error alpha_cell
The claimed coverage premise accounts for fitting/candidate/evaluation randomness
statements.conclusion: The compound radius epsilon+min(2,sqrt(2 log(2/delta)/m)) covers population benefit with probability >=1-alpha_cell-delta and bounds the union of directional errors by alpha_cell+delta.

proof_authority.summary: Apply width-two Hoeffding conditionally, average, intersect with cell coverage, and use a union bound and triangle inequality. No independence between the two good events is required.

formal_correspondence.boundary: Independent-sampling concentration and deterministic compound-interval soundness are mechanized separately. Conditional-episode integration, the clipped sampling radius, extended radii, and the joint conformal/union-bound capstone are not one identical registered theorem.

edge_cases: The radius cap 2 is valid because both population and cell benefits lie in [-1,1].
m=0 is outside the formula and must be explicitly excluded.
No concentration claim is inherited by macro-F1.
Small sample size can make all decisions abstain without showing impossibility.

statements.title: Failure of automatic cell-to-population transfer
assumptions: Two inputs with probabilities 0.45 and 0.55 and deterministic labels 1 and 0
Fixed f0=0 and fa=1
One-item iid evaluation cell and fixed input-only h(a)=1,h(b)=-1
statements.conclusion: Perfect cell coverage with zero radius coexists with negative population benefit -0.10 and ADAPT probability 0.45.

proof_authority.summary: Frozen and adapted risks are 0.45 and 0.55. The input-only predictor equals the realized one-item accuracy contrast and adapts exactly at a.

formal_correspondence.boundary: Exact finite constructive proof checked manually. Existing unit-mismatch Lean lemmas are related but do not encode this specific probability model and numbers.

edge_cases: The predictor is fixed in the existence construction; no algorithm is claimed to learn its perfect mapping without relevant historical information.
The same example has d=1,M=0,gamma=-0.05, emphasizing differing targets/units.

statements.title: Finite-sample population benefit certificate
assumptions: Protocol P1: predictor/feature fitting frozen before calibration
Protocol P2: calibration and deployment episodes exchangeable conditional on development data
Protocol P3: candidate constructed from separate adaptation inputs and frozen before scoring
Protocol P4: positive integer m fresh conditionally iid evaluation observations independent of adaptation
Protocol P5: paired accuracy difference is the covered target
N>=0 calibration episodes; alpha_cell,delta in (0,1) with alpha_cell+delta<1
Conformal rank k=ceil((N+1)(1-alpha_cell)); k>N produces infinity
statements.conclusion: Split conformal cell coverage plus fresh-sample Hoeffding yields population-benefit coverage and joint strict-direction error budget alpha_cell+delta.

proof_authority.summary: Conditional exchangeability gives residual coverage including ties. Width-two Hoeffding gives population concentration. Union bound and event containment complete the argument without independence of the two good events.

formal_correspondence.boundary: The finite random conformal threshold, independent Hoeffding, and deterministic action modules supply components. No single registered theorem instantiates conditional episode sampling, actual order-statistic measurability including infinity, and compound coverage from P1-P5. Real benchmark premises remain external.

edge_cases: N=0 or unavailable rank yields an infinite radius and abstention.
Ties are conservative, not grounds for clipping the rank.
Nonempty m is necessary for the sample mean.
Candidate reuse/selection on scoring inputs invalidates the fresh fixed-pair argument.

statements.title: Sampled population frontier
assumptions: Binary labels and zero-one loss
Fixed measurable model pair and score s in [0,1]
Positive target disagreement mass d
Measurable target correctness kernel
Nonnegative fixed sample size m; iid target inputs independent of fixed predictor pair and score
For d>0, the true target belongs to the externally justified residual class C_beta
alpha in (0,1); abstain when observed n_D=0
statements.conclusion: Strict sampled-margin rules have each wrong-direction probability at most alpha (and the union also at most alpha).

proof_authority.summary: Conditional on each realized positive n_D, ordered selected disagreement inputs are iid from mu_T conditioned on D. Width-one Hoeffding gives the displayed radius; average over counts and use abstention at zero count. On margin coverage the population sign follows from the external beta bound.

formal_correspondence.boundary: The generic independent-mean bound and population frontier are registered. The random disagreement-count thinning/disintegration and this combined sampled decision rule are LaTeX proof steps, not one identical Lean capstone.

edge_cases: Condition on each n_D=k>0, not merely the aggregate event n_D>0.
n_D=0 must abstain; d=0 has zero population benefit and no defined conditional M.
Reusing evidence to fit s or choose f_a is outside the stated fixed-predictor sampling setup.
Fixed-size marginal validity does not license optional stopping.

statements.title: Conditional paired-benefit coverage
assumptions: Finite fixed prediction bins and classes, including zero-count bins
Both predictors fixed independently of source/target evidence samples
Within each source class, iid conditional observations with fixed or conditioned-on counts
Iid target joint-prediction observations
Valid exact two-sided Clopper-Pearson boxes allocated alpha/(RK+R), including [0,1] for absent source classes
Externally justified aggregate conditional-TV bound rho>=0; 0<alpha<1
Exact LP extrema on the stated compact polytope, with abstention on empty sets
statements.conclusion: The true paired population benefit is enclosed with probability at least 1-alpha, and strict sign errors have marginal probability at most alpha.

proof_authority.summary: Union-bound source-conditional and target-marginal interval containment. On this event the true prior/table and s=A pi, v=|t-s| meet all LP constraints under the external TV budget, so extrema contain the objective.

formal_correspondence.boundary: No registered complete Lean encoding covers binomial intervals, TV model, LP extrema or numerical quantiles. The exact-statistical theorem is separate from numerical inverse-beta endpoints and binary64 weak-dual objective bounds.

edge_cases: Zero source class count supplies [0,1], not invented observations.
pi_y=0 causes no division in coverage; sharpness requires a feasible normalized source column for zero-mass classes.
No invertibility assumption is needed.
On interval containment the exact polytope cannot be empty.
Empty or numerically suspect output causes abstention.
Joint binomial coverage does not require multinomial entries to be independent.

supporting_claims.review: Intersection of valid correctness interval and the residual bound; constant eta=z+1/2 attains every z. Closed interval nonempty for feasible M and beta>=0.

For M>=0 the feasible residual endpoint -beta is available; for M<=0 the endpoint +beta is available. For general beta the maximum absolute feasible residual is min(beta,1/2+|M|), so unrestricted equality to beta would be false.

supporting_claims.claim: k=ceil((n+1)(1-alpha)), using +infinity if k>n, yields residual coverage under joint exchangeability.
supporting_claims.review: Finite-rank threshold miss probability <=(n+1-k)/(n+1)<=alpha. Ties are conservative. The unbounded branch covers any finite residual. Outcome-disjointness alone does not imply score exchangeability.

supporting_claims.claim: The exact three-class example has interval [.2,.8] at rho=0; the smallest transport budget allowing nonpositive benefit is 1/6.
supporting_claims.review: Let prior=(a,b,g). Third-class mass costs at least g to move out of its original row. Removing the initial helpful mass .2a+.8b minus possible harmful mass g costs at least max(0,.2a+.8b-g) in the first two columns. Thus total cost >=max(g,.2a+.8b)>=max(g,.2(1-g))>=1/6. The printed table attains equality and zero benefit.

supporting_claims.claim: The common-polytope paired interval [.1,.4] is tighter than subtracting separate accuracy intervals [-.1,.6].
supporting_claims.review: With prior=(p,1-p,0), adapted accuracy=.4+.2p and frozen accuracy=.5p; their difference=.4-.3p. Individual extrema are [.4,.6] and [0,.5]. Reassigning labels to frozen predictions yields paired benefit -.5 while preserving observed bins and violating rho=0.

supporting_claims.claim: For feasible x in [0,1], Bx<=b, Ex=d and lambda<=0, objective is at least b^T lambda+d^T mu+sum min(0,c-B^T lambda-E^T mu).
supporting_claims.review: Write c^T x=lambda^T Bx+mu^T Ex+r^T x. The sign of lambda gives lambda^T Bx>=lambda^T b, and each r_j x_j>=min(0,r_j). This bounds any exact feasible point; it does not prove feasible points exist or exact binomial endpoints were supplied.

supporting_claims.claim: Nine identical random fair signs are exchangeable and globally symmetric, yet independent-coordinate sign-flip enumeration is not valid.
supporting_claims.review: All-positive occurs with probability 1/2, but only one of 2^9 independent sign assignments has a mean at least the all-positive mean. The resulting one-sided reference p=1/512 is anticonservative; coordinatewise sign symmetry is the missing condition.

historical_exclusions.description: One selected representative per label-swap orbit does not ensure evidence-fibre sign consistency. Do not resurrect the original claim.
Corrected Boolean fibre consistency gives set-theoretic factorization; it does not prove a measurable decoder on arbitrary spaces.
Only propagation under an explicitly supplied nonnegative domination contract is proved. Estimation of H and empirical domination validity remain outside this result.
